prompt.content:
Step: PLAN SPLIT (round 1). Propose the first split of the property: where does the hardness come from (which index, pointer or slot does the proof quantify over)? Each piece is first checked with a 3 s cap, 8 pieces at a time; pieces that time out come back to you with timings.

Signals:
srFull  width 1  wire
srEmpty  width 1  wire
srDataOut  width 4  wire
rst  width 1  input
rbFull  width 1  wire
rbEmpty  width 1  wire
rbDataOut  width 4  wire
push  width 1  input
pop  width 1  input
equal  width 1  wire
dataIn  width 4  input
bb_first  width 1  register
sr_dataOut  width 4  wire
sr_empty  width 1  register
sr_full  width 1  wire
sr_tail  width 4  register
rb_dataOut  width 4  wire
rb_empty  width 1  register
rb_full  width 1  wire
rb_head  width 4  register
rb_tail  width 4  register
prop_a  width 1  wire
prop_en  width 1  wire
sr_mem_0 .. sr_mem_15 and rb_mem_0 .. rb_mem_15: registers, width 4 (the FIFO storage)

Answer: {"split":<explicit cases or index direction>,"reason":"..."}

raw_response: {"split":{"index":"rb_tail","bits":1,"auto":true},"reason":"The check 'equal' compares sr_mem[sr_tail] against rb_mem[rb_tail] plus the full/empty flags; the real hardness is the pointer arithmetic of the FIFOs, i.e. the proof quantifies over the index registers that select which memory slot is read/written (rb_tail, rb_head, sr_tail). Instantiating these pointers turns the all-slots data equality into a concrete slot comparison. Start by case-splitting the ring-buffer tail pointer rb_tail on its top bit (2 cases), with auto:true so the tool keeps splitting the remaining bits of rb_tail on the children that time out; later rounds can fix rb_head/sr_tail the same way. Splitting on outputs (full/empty/equal) is avoided since it would not instantiate the quantified index."}

extra_input.reason: The check 'equal' compares sr_mem[sr_tail] against rb_mem[rb_tail] plus the full/empty flags; the real hardness is the pointer arithmetic of the FIFOs, i.e. the proof quantifies over the index registers that select which memory slot is read/written (rb_tail, rb_head, sr_tail). Instantiating these pointers turns the all-slots data equality into a concrete slot comparison. Start by case-splitting the ring-buffer tail pointer rb_tail on its top bit (2 cases), with auto:true so the tool keeps splitting the remaining bits of rb_tail on the children that time out; later rounds can fix rb_head/sr_tail the same way. Splitting on outputs (full/empty/equal) is avoided since it would not instantiate the quantified index.
